policy.note: Source trust labels and catalog review claims are not inherited by this registry.

decision.reason: Bounded pre-data-collection scope and deterministic scripts are useful, but assumptions, power claims, and dependencies require method review.
Local citation and claim checks align with the integrity layer; semantic scientific review must remain separate.
Its request planning, failure classification, normalization, and open-source fallback are useful; the accepted tool port must not privilege one endpoint or upload data without policy negotiation.
Location, evidence basis, coverage denominator, and residual-risk gates are useful integrity patterns; the full thesis workflow is too broad and contains upload assumptions.
Writing and response templates may be useful later, but drafting, review, grants, and submission should not be admitted as one global Skill.
Stable hypothesis and review IDs are useful; a fixed seven-stage pipeline and paper-count thresholds should not become a cross-discipline global research process.
Its input/output/sample/baseline decomposition is valuable, but the bundled workflow is too broad for one reusable skill.
Deterministic metadata filtering is useful. The embedded 1391-entry catalog remains an unverified discovery source, not an admission decision.
Trigger, non-trigger, boundary, and with/without tests are useful; a critic agent must not become a permanent recursive control plane.
The skill sends research content to a hardcoded public HTTP service and binds execution to one provider family.
Presentation production is not a current research-kernel need and this single skill imposes excessive instruction context.
Persistent cognitive profiling increases privacy and context risks without improving the research object model.

Figure specifications, lineage, and visual gates may be useful, but the package uploads research content to a hardcoded plain-HTTP service, reads credentials, invokes external models, and can execute repair scripts.

Animation output and render checks are useful optional patterns, but cloning a runtime, installing dependencies, binding one provider, and executing generated Manim code do not belong in the research kernel.
Separating deployment, protocol, behavior, and maintenance evidence is useful; executing arbitrary packages and adding another AI critic would increase supply-chain and recursive review costs.
Course and video production is not a research-method or integrity need for the current workbench and would add a large external media toolchain.

Fact, number, citation, and evidence-strength locks are useful design constraints, but the unlicensed source package is not vendored; an independently implemented repository candidate carries the evaluation work.

The independently implemented candidate is bounded, offline, and deterministically checks surface invariants, but it remains outside runtime discovery until semantic drift and incremental value are measured on representative tasks.
Operating a social account, engagement loop, and points system is unrelated to research quality and introduces persistent external identity and write-side effects.
The metadata, DOI, BibTeX, validation, and opt-in write patterns are valuable, but discovery, enrichment, and validation must be split and provider assumptions removed.
The provenance objective is useful, but every paper value cannot reliably link to a mutable code line; only the problem pattern may inform an independent design.
Useful for skill packaging conventions; it is not a research method and is not copied into the runtime.
Useful for understanding Codex skill structure and source discipline; provider-specific content stays outside the research kernel.
Evidence and retry discipline are useful; self-scoring thresholds and self-learning loops should not become global architecture.
Typed support, contradiction, qualification, missing-evidence, and exact-locator contracts align strongly with the project evidence model.
The file-selection checklist is useful, but it adds no stable method beyond the existing read allowlist and context-governance contract.
Conversion is deterministic tooling, not a research judgment Skill; retain limitations and explicit output policy in a capability card.
PDF conversion belongs in a renderer/parser adapter and does not add enough judgment to justify a standalone research Skill.
Word conversion is a deterministic adapter concern; output location and format limitations must be explicit.
The reusable part is a conversion script and render check, not a research workflow Skill.
The stable local core plus dynamic official lookup pattern is useful for MCP and tool bindings, but the Skill is vendor-specific and redundant as an authoring baseline.
This is a persistent knowledge subsystem rather than a bounded Skill and would duplicate provenance, artifact, and context-governance layers.
Requesting missing files is part of the Task/read-scope protocol and does not need independent Skill discovery.
Pre-data design, pseudoreplication, randomization, and blocking are valuable, but discipline-specific assumptions and human method approval are mandatory.
Scope, search, screening, extraction, and synthesis patterns are useful; fixed services, database counts, and forced figure generation are not portable requirements.
Confidentiality, authorization, evidence separation, and accountable review are strong; venue-specific rules and autonomous editorial authority must be excluded.
Source packets and counterevidence fields are useful; fixed APIs, model names, and a target of sixty references must not enter the portable core.
Honest encodings, accessibility, provenance, explicit exports, and inspection gates provide clear value when separated from plotting-library adapters.
No-fabrication, evidence binding, and authorship boundaries are useful, but the monolithic workflow duplicates the workbench claim and handoff architecture.
Assumptions, effect sizes, and reproducibility are useful, but one generic Skill cannot safely route frequentist, Bayesian, and domain-specific analyses.
Its effect-size, sensitivity, observed-power, clustering, attrition, and simulation warnings are valuable when bound to an approved design and explicit assumptions.
The traceability objective is useful, but requiring every formula and code module to map one-to-one is not generally valid.
The implementation reads credentials from a hardcoded local file and passes them into commands; only the general citation validation problem may inform an independent design.
The statistical routing is too generic and the fixed four-reviewer process adds coordination cost without method-specific assurance.
Ablation sequencing may be useful for ML cases, but the implementation-tuning-improvement recipe is not a general experimental design method.
Persona dialogue creates token-heavy correlated review; query-angle diversification can be implemented directly without preserving the workflow.
Hardcoded credential discovery and paths are unsafe; provider-neutral search and ranking contracts must be designed independently.
The entry is too generic to establish incremental Skill value; its headings may inform a theory-task action checklist.
A bounded search can report closest overlaps and residual uncertainty, but an agent cannot reliably certify novelty with a binary verdict.
Concern-to-section-to-action-to-verification mapping is useful, but acceptance, extra experiments, and unresolved disagreements remain human decisions.
Three simulated reviewers and averaged scores do not provide independent review evidence and can produce misleading editorial authority.
The sketch lacks a safe evaluator, units and dimensional checks, and a validated execution contract; it should not be tested generically.
Human ownership, reality gates, claim states, and plan-depth limits align with the workbench, but the full research lifecycle must not load as one global Skill.
Root-cause evidence and one-variable hypothesis tests are useful for engineering, but the iron-law workflow should not govern every research task.
Fresh evidence before completion claims is a stable invariant and deterministic Gate, not an optional Skill that should consume discovery context.
Baseline failure, pressure scenarios, and wording microtests are useful; test repetition and process depth must scale with risk, variance, and budget rather than apply universally.
